chill.title: Coffee at Cxffeeblack's Mitchell Heights Flagship
chill.description: A newly opened roastery and café built around reclaiming the Black history of coffee, with an East African ceremony tradition and a tripled roasting capacity.
chill.bonus: Ask about the Ethiopian lot they're pouring and where it was bought.

chill.title: Shelby Farms Lakeside Afternoon
chill.description: A park five times the size of Central Park, with a lake loop, buffalo in a paddock and enough space that it never feels busy.
chill.bonus: Walk the full Hyde Lake loop and find the bison herd on the way.

chill.title: Rainbow Lake and the Overton Greensward
chill.description: The open lawn and small lake at the heart of Overton Park, where Midtown spends its evenings with blankets and dogs and no particular plan.
chill.bonus: Bring something to sit on and stay until the light goes completely.

chill.title: Cooper-Young Browse
chill.description: A late-Victorian neighbourhood of bungalows and independent shops around one intersection, marked by a welded steel trestle gateway over the street.
chill.bonus: Find the trestle and pick out the hidden objects welded into it.

chill.title: Dixon Gallery and Gardens
chill.description: French Impressionists and a good German porcelain collection in a Georgian-style house on seventeen acres of woodland garden in East Memphis.
chill.bonus: Do the gardens before the house. Most people do it the wrong way round.

chill.title: Elmwood Cemetery on Foot
chill.description: Eighty acres of Victorian garden cemetery from 1852, with an audio tour, enormous magnolias and the graves of yellow fever nurses and blues musicians.
chill.bonus: Take the audio tour and find the 1878 yellow fever section.

chill.title: Bluff Walk Along River Garden
chill.description: A landscaped stretch of the Memphis bluff walk between Beale Street Landing and the cobblestones, with swings facing the water.
chill.bonus: Sit on the bluff swings and watch one full barge convoy go past.

chill.title: Sunset Over the Bridge from the Cobblestones
chill.description: The restored nineteenth-century cobblestone landing at the foot of Monroe, where the Hernando de Soto bridge lights up in sequence after dark.
chill.bonus: Stay for the full bridge light sequence once it starts.

chill.title: Memphis Botanic Garden Morning
chill.description: Ninety-six acres and thirty collections in East Memphis, including a Japanese garden with a drum bridge and a rose garden that peaks twice a year.
chill.bonus: Sit on the bridge in the Japanese garden until someone else arrives.

chill.title: The Peabody Duck March
chill.description: Twice a day since the 1930s, five mallards ride the elevator down and walk a red carpet to the lobby fountain, led by a uniformed Duckmaster.
chill.bonus: Get a seat at the lobby bar an hour early. It fills up completely.

social.title: A Set at the Green Room, Crosstown Arts
social.description: A small listening room inside the old Sears tower, programmed with jazz, blues and experimental acts and treated as a room where you actually listen.
social.bonus: Sit in the front row and don't talk through the set.

social.title: Beale Street End to End
social.description: Three blocks that produced more of American music than any other street, still running live bands out of every doorway from afternoon until very late.
social.bonus: Stop in the smallest room on the street and tip the band properly.

social.title: Thirty Years of Blues at Rum Boogie
social.description: A Beale Street room hung with hundreds of signed guitars, running live blues seven nights a week for three decades.
social.bonus: Find the most famous guitar on the ceiling and work out whose it is.

social.title: Live Music at Lafayette's, Overton Square
social.description: The reopened version of the 1970s room that launched Big Star and gave Billy Joel early stages, running local and touring acts most nights.
social.bonus: Get a table on the balcony above the stage.

social.title: Soul Burger and the Jukebox at Earnestine & Hazel's
social.description: A former pharmacy and brothel on South Main, reopened under new ownership, with a legendary jukebox upstairs that people swear plays itself.
social.bonus: Go upstairs alone, put a dollar in the jukebox and see what happens.

social.title: Disco Until Three at Paula & Raiford's
social.description: A two-storey basement club on Second Street with leather couches, fog, disco balls and handprints on the wall, open Friday and Saturday only.
social.bonus: Get your handprint on the wall before you leave.

social.title: Rooftop Cocktails at Hu. Roof
social.description: Seventeen floors up on Madison Avenue, indoor and outdoor, looking straight down the river at the Hernando de Soto bridge.
social.bonus: Be up there for sunset and stay for the bridge lights.

social.title: Pints at Wiseacre's Downtown HQ
social.description: A 40,000 square foot brewery and taproom on B.B. King Boulevard with a hundred-thousand-barrel capacity and food partners in the building.
social.bonus: Drink the Tiny Bomb and the Ananda back to back and pick a favourite.

social.title: Live Blues at B.B. King's
social.description: The original of the B.B. King's clubs, opened on Beale in 1991, with a house band that is genuinely excellent and music every single day.
social.bonus: Stay for a full set by the house band, not just two songs.

social.title: Grizzlies Night at FedExForum
social.description: An NBA crowd that plays up the Grit and Grind identity harder than any other building in the league, two blocks off Beale.
social.bonus: Stay in your seat through the whole fourth quarter no matter the score.

social.title: Whiskey Tour at Old Dominick
social.description: A forty-five minute grain-to-glass tour of a revived 1866 Memphis distillery on Front Street, ending in a guided tasting of the full range.
social.bonus: Buy the bottle you liked least and see if it grows on you.

social.title: The Last Juke Joint: Wild Bill's
social.description: A cinder-block room on Vollintine Avenue with long communal tables, quart bottles of beer and the Juke Joint Allstars playing until dawn.
social.bonus: Sit at a shared table with strangers and stay past two in the morning.

culture.title: Blues Hall of Fame
culture.description: A small, dense museum across from the Civil Rights Museum, with individual galleries for each inductee and listening stations for the recordings.
culture.bonus: Pick one inductee you've never heard of and listen to all of their tracks.

culture.title: Slave Haven Underground Railroad Museum
culture.description: The 1849 Burkle Estate on North Second, a clapboard house with trap doors and a cellar used to shelter people escaping north.
culture.bonus: Go down into the cellar and stay long enough to understand the scale of it.

culture.title: Memphis Rock 'n' Soul Museum
culture.description: A Smithsonian-developed collection tracing how sharecropper music became rock and soul, in a building on the corner of Beale at FedExForum.
culture.bonus: Use the audio guide fully — there are over a hundred songs on it.

culture.title: Sun Studio
culture.description: The small storefront on Union Avenue where Sam Phillips recorded Elvis, Johnny Cash, Carl Perkins and Howlin' Wolf, still standing and still working.
culture.bonus: Hold the original microphone when they offer it. Everyone should.

culture.title: National Civil Rights Museum at the Lorraine
culture.description: The Lorraine Motel, with Room 306 preserved and the balcony exactly as it was on 4 April 1968, at the end of a full history of the movement.
culture.bonus: Give it three hours. Two is not enough and you will feel that.

culture.title: The Metal Museum's New Overton Park Home
culture.description: The national metal arts museum reopened in September 2026 in the old Memphis College of Art building after a $35 million, ten-year move.
culture.bonus: Find the working smithy and watch someone actually forge something.

culture.title: Stax Museum of American Soul Music
culture.description: Built on the site of the original Stax studio in Soulsville, with Isaac Hayes' gold-trimmed Cadillac and a rebuilt sloping-floor recording room.
culture.bonus: Stand in the reconstructed Studio A and notice the floor is on a slope.

culture.title: Graceland
culture.description: Elvis Presley's house, kept as it was in 1977, from the jungle room to the racquetball building, plus the jets and the car museum across the road.
culture.bonus: Stand at the Meditation Garden for a minute without taking a photo.

8ball.title: Wildcard: The Barbecue Bracket
8ball.description: Four barbecue joints, one day, one item each — pick a winner by knockout and argue it out at every round.
8ball.bonus: No repeating an order. Whoever loses the argument drives.

8ball.title: Wildcard: Follow the Music
8ball.description: Start on Beale and follow whatever music you can hear from the street — every time you can hear a different band, you have to go in.
8ball.bonus: Four rooms minimum, and you tip in every single one.

adventure.title: Sightseeing Cruise with Memphis Riverboats
adventure.description: Ninety minutes out on the Mississippi on a paddlewheeler, past Presidents Island and the Wolf River tributary with the bluffs above you.
adventure.bonus: Stand at the bow for the turn and feel how fast the current actually is.

adventure.title: Ride the Hampline to Crosstown
adventure.description: A protected bike lane running from Overton Park through Binghampton, connecting the park, the Greenline and the old Sears tower at Crosstown.
adventure.bonus: Finish inside Crosstown Concourse and ride the freight elevator up.

adventure.title: Sunset in Tom Lee Park
adventure.description: Thirty acres of rebuilt riverfront park on the bluff, opened in 2023, facing due west across the widest water in the country.
adventure.bonus: Find the Tom Lee monument and read what he actually did in 1925.

adventure.title: Walk the Big River Crossing at Sunset
adventure.description: The longest pedestrian bridge across the Mississippi, a mile of boardwalk bolted to the side of the 1916 Harahan rail bridge, lit at night and free to cross.
adventure.bonus: Walk all the way into Arkansas and back so you can say you did.

adventure.title: Treetop Adventure at Go Ape
adventure.description: Ziplines, rope bridges and Tarzan swings strung through the woods of Shelby Farms, one of the largest urban parks in the country.
adventure.bonus: Do the Tarzan swing without pausing at the top. Just go.

adventure.title: Bike the Wolf River Greenway
adventure.description: A paved greenway following the Wolf River corridor through bottomland forest, connecting Midtown to the eastern suburbs without crossing traffic.
adventure.bonus: Ride until the path runs out, whichever direction you pick.

adventure.title: Memphis Zoo Morning
adventure.description: Seventy-six acres in Overton Park with a serious big cat collection and an aquarium, best done in the first two hours after opening.
adventure.bonus: Get to the big cats first, before the heat puts them to sleep.

adventure.title: Shelby Farms Greenline to Downtown
adventure.description: Eleven miles of converted rail line running dead straight from Shelby Farms Park into Midtown, flat the whole way and shaded most of it.
adventure.bonus: Ride the full length one way and get a ride back with the bikes.

adventure.title: Old Forest Loop in Overton Park
adventure.description: A hundred and fifty acres of genuine old-growth forest that the city fought the interstate system to keep, right in the middle of Midtown.
adventure.bonus: Walk the whole loop without leaving the tree cover once.

adventure.title: Kayak Hyde Lake at Shelby Farms
adventure.description: Eighty acres of flat water in the middle of a 4,500-acre park, with boats to rent at the lakeside and herons working the shoreline.
adventure.bonus: Paddle the full perimeter of the lake without cutting a corner.

adventure.title: Hike the Chickasaw Bluffs at Meeman-Shelby
adventure.description: Thirteen thousand acres of bottomland hardwood on the Mississippi north of the city, with steep loess bluffs and two lakes nobody seems to know about.
adventure.bonus: Take the Woodland Trail down to the river bottom and back up the bluff.

adventure.title: Paddle the Ghost River Section
adventure.description: A stretch of the Wolf River where the channel disappears entirely into a tupelo swamp and you follow white markers nailed to the trees to find your way.
adventure.bonus: Stop paddling in the middle of the swamp and sit in total silence for five minutes.

adventure.title: Axe Throwing at Go Ape
adventure.description: Outdoor lanes at Shelby Farms where you throw hand axes at wooden targets under instruction, which is harder and more satisfying than it looks.
adventure.bonus: First person to stick three in a row picks where you eat afterwards.

adventure.title: Chucalissa Mounds at T.O. Fuller
adventure.description: A reconstructed Mississippian village and platform mound occupied until around 1500, inside a state park on the bluffs south-west of the city.
adventure.bonus: Climb the platform mound and look at what the chief would have seen.

adventure.title: The Lookout at the Pyramid
adventure.description: A glass elevator up the inside of a 32-storey pyramid — once an arena, now a Bass Pro store with a cypress swamp in the lobby — to an observation deck over the river.
adventure.bonus: Walk the full outdoor deck and find the Lorraine Motel from up there.

adventure.title: Climb at Memphis Rox
adventure.description: The largest non-profit climbing gym in the world, on McLemore Avenue in South Memphis, which turns nobody away for inability to pay.
adventure.bonus: Get to the top of a route you're sure you can't finish.

foodie.title: Dry Ribs at Charlie Vergos' Rendezvous
foodie.description: A basement off Second Street where, in 1948, Charlie Vergos turned an old elevator shaft into a smoker and invented the Memphis dry rub.
foodie.bonus: Order the dry ribs and don't ask for sauce. They will notice.

foodie.title: Wet Ribs at Central BBQ Downtown
foodie.description: The other side of the Memphis rib argument, three minutes' walk from the Civil Rights Museum, with a patio and a smoke line you can smell from the street.
foodie.bonus: Order wet ribs here and dry at the Rendezvous on the same trip. Decide.

foodie.title: World Food at Global Café
foodie.description: A food hall inside Crosstown Concourse run as a social enterprise by immigrant and refugee chefs, cooking Venezuelan, Sudanese and Mexican dishes from scratch.
foodie.bonus: Order from all three kitchens and split everything three ways.

foodie.title: Chopped Pork at Payne's Bar-B-Que
foodie.description: A painted cement-block shop on Lamar, open since 1972, doing a chopped pork sandwich with mustard slaw that a lot of people will tell you is the best in America.
foodie.bonus: Get there before one. They close at two and they run out.

foodie.title: Fried Chicken at Gus's on Front Street
foodie.description: The downtown room that turned a small-town Tennessee recipe into a forty-location legend: dark, spiced, shattering crust and meat that's still juicy.
foodie.bonus: Order the white meat plate and the fried pickles and nothing else.

foodie.title: Breakfast at The Arcade
foodie.description: Memphis' oldest café, open since 1919 on the South Main trolley line, with vinyl booths, sweet potato pancakes and a corner table Elvis used.
foodie.bonus: Ask which booth was his and sit in it if it's free.

foodie.title: Fried Green Tomatoes at Alcenia's
foodie.description: A small bright North Main room run for twenty-five years by B.J. Chester-Tamayo, recently reopened after a long renovation, where you may get hugged on the way in.
foodie.bonus: Take whatever the dessert of the day is without asking what it is.

foodie.title: Deep-Fried Cheeseburger at Dyer's
foodie.description: A Beale Street counter that claims to have been straining and reusing the same grease since 1912, which is either revolting or magnificent.
foodie.bonus: Order the double and ask them about the grease. They love the question.

foodie.title: Soul Food Plate at The Four Way
foodie.description: Open since 1946 in Soulsville, a few blocks from Stax, and a meeting place during the civil rights movement — Dr. King ate here regularly.
foodie.bonus: Get the fried catfish and the peach cobbler. Both, not one.

foodie.title: Smoked Everything at Elwood's Shack
foodie.description: A converted shack behind a Summer Avenue strip mall doing barbecue, tacos, fish and pizza at once, and somehow doing all of it well.
foodie.bonus: Order the thing on the menu that makes least sense next to the others.

foodie.title: Barbecue Cornish Hen at Cozy Corner
foodie.description: A North Parkway room open since 1977 where the thing to order isn't ribs at all — it's a whole smoked Cornish game hen.
foodie.bonus: Order the hen, not the ribs. That's the entire point of coming.

foodie.title: Burger and a Beer at Huey's Downtown
foodie.description: The flagship of a Memphis chain since 1970, on Second Street, where the tradition is to shoot toothpicks into the ceiling and nobody stops you.
foodie.bonus: Get a toothpick to stick in the ceiling before you leave.
